source.title: Style transfer-based image synthesis as an efficient regularization technique in deep learning

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Compares a data augmentation intervention and its no-additional-augmentation baseline on held-out classification AUC, a different measure of generalization from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study compares style-transfer data augmentation with no additional data augmentation. Dropout, ordinary augmentation, and early stopping are applied to every network; their individual effects are not tested. Results cited from other studies are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates its own style-transfer training method. It uses dropout in every condition without testing dropout's effect, and its results do not test any of V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' stated conclusion: they claim a 2.68% average AUC improvement and recommend using their method alongside other regularization techniques. However, Table I contradicts that improvement and the prose's stated VGG16 decrease, so the conclusion is not supported by the table as labeled.
record.recipe_differences: Uses style-transfer-generated pseudo-labeled skin lesion images for training and real images for validation and testing; this is not the random-label, optimizer, batch-size, dropout comparison, sharpness measurement, or example-removal recipe in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported AUC change differs by architecture: VGG16 improves with augmentation, while VGG9, VGG11, and DenseNet121 have lower reported average AUC with augmentation.

fits_no_version.finding: Under Table I's condition labels, style-transfer training lowers average AUC for VGG9, VGG11 and DenseNet121, and raises it for VGG16. The accompanying prose reports the opposite overall direction and a VGG16 decrease.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training on style-transfer-generated, pseudo-labeled skin lesion images changes held-out AUC relative to conventional training, with architecture-dependent outcomes; the reported direction is internally inconsistent.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Methods & Models in Automation & Robotics
record.problems: The text does not report uncertainty estimates. It reports AUC rather than train-to-test error gaps, and style-transfer augmentation is evaluated alongside other regularization techniques applied to every network.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and compensating recipe changes.
All dropout effects: dropout is used in every condition, with no dropout ablation or joint dropout-and-weight-decay removal.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Retain the table values as printed; the supplied text cannot establish whether the table's condition labels or the narrative are wrong. Comparisons among VGG depths do not test V2, and noisy pseudo-labels without a memorization measurement do not test V1.

versions.untested_parts: Network width relative to the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and tuning conditions.
Dropout is applied in every condition; the study does not compare dropout settings or its effect.
Sharpness measures and their relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: VGG9
rows.operation_detail: Trained with style-transfer data augmentation in addition to traditional augmentation, dropout, and early stopping.
rows.note: The paper identifies this as AUC; its reported fold values are 0.805, 0.820, 0.845, 0.845, 0.805 with style-transfer augmentation and 0.835, 0.880, 0.845, 0.875, 0.850 without it. The reported average is lower with augmentation.
rows.check: Own-method comparison, not evidence for a listed version. Table I reports AUC decreasing from 0.857 to 0.824. The intervention trains on synthetic pseudo-labeled images rather than simply adding images to the original training set. The baseline retains traditional augmentation.

rows.subject: VGG11
rows.operation_detail: Trained with style-transfer data augmentation in addition to traditional augmentation, dropout, and early stopping.

rows.check: Own-method comparison, not evidence for a listed version. Table I reports AUC decreasing from 0.861 to 0.822. The intervention replaces real training images with synthetic pseudo-labeled images; the baseline retains traditional augmentation.
